subject: Service disruption: regional cloud outage and temporary traffic diversion
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara@novapay.finance>, ops@novapay.finance
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-02T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service disruption: regional cloud outage and temporary traffic diversion

Hi Sara / NovaPay ops team,

We’re reaching out to notify you that between ~07:48 UTC and ongoing we observed a regional outage affecting cloud provider interconnects in US-EAST and intermittent degradation in EU-WEST. Symptoms we saw: elevated 5xx errors for inference endpoints, increased tail latency (p95 -> ~900ms), and some streaming connections dropped.

Immediate mitigations we’ve applied on our side:
- Automatic traffic diversion enabled to route requests from impacted regions to healthy capacity in US-WEST and EU-CENTRAL.
- Read-only fallback endpoints enabled for non-critical batching jobs.
- Increased prefix/KV cache TTL to reduce token compute.

Recommended actions for NovaPay (short checklist):
- If you manage routing on your side, set your Redwood routing policy to prefer region=us-west,eu-central for the next 6–12 hours.
- Lower DNS TTL to 60s if you need faster cutover (only if you control DNS).
- If you use pinned capacity, consider enabling cross-region fallback in the console under Project → Deployment → Fallback policy.

I’ve attached a short playbook with CLI snippets and a sample reroute config: traffic-diversion-playbook.pdf (attachment).

We’ll keep the status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-06-02-region-outage. I’m monitoring with the SRE team and will escalate if the provider reports broader impact. Please reply here if you want us to schedule a short call to walk through the reroute steps.

—
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Service disruption: regional cloud outage and temporary traffic diversion

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick Q: we control the DNS in front of the Redwood endpoint. Is the recommendation to lower our global TTL to 60s now, and then raise it once you confirm full recovery? Any preference around how long you expect cross-region warmup to take (we have short-lived sessions that are sensitive to cold starts).

Also, please include the exact name of the fallback endpoint/host so our infra team can add it to the routing policy.

—
Sara
Head of Infrastructure, NovaPay
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-03T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: outage timeline & initial RCA draft (please review)

Team —

I’m attaching the raw timeline and initial RCA bullets (outage-timeline.csv). Summary: at 07:47 UTC the cloud provider reported an interconnect flap impacting traffic through their us-east exchange. We observed increased packet loss and TCP retransmits starting ~07:50 UTC which cascaded into connection resets for long-lived streaming sessions. Automatic routing rules in the provider attempted local failover but introduced transient routing loops for a subset of flows; that produced the 5xx spike.

Mitigations applied:
- 07:55 UTC: We toggled provider-level prefer-other-region for affected capacity pools.
- 08:03 UTC: Enabled our cross-region diversion to us-west / eu-central and scaled up dedicated instances for critical SLAs.
- 08:18 UTC: Increased cache TTL and temporarily disabled prefetch to lower downstream pressure.

Open action items:
1) Short: publish customer-facing reroute hostnames and a one-pager for DNS steps (owner: Lauren).
2) Mid: add health-check threshold that triggers diversion earlier (owner: Marcus).
3) Long: add automated cross-region warmup (pre-warm GPUs) for hot customers (owner: Hannah + infra).

Notes: we should consider issuing a small account credit for accounts with >2 hours impact. I’ll draft the internal RCA section; Hannah, can you confirm the proposed credit floor?

Jonas
Senior SRE
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-03T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: outage timeline & initial RCA draft (please review)

Thanks Jonas — quick confirmations:
- I support the short/mid/long action split. Marcus, please give ETA on health-check threshold change (we should target 5 business days).
- For credits: propose automatic credit for affected customers prorated by downtime beyond 30 minutes; manual review above $5k. Lauren, please surface which accounts cross that line (I think NovaPay and Acme Retail reach it).
- Schedule: I’ll host a 30-minute postmortem review tomorrow at 11am PT; invite will go to all on this thread plus product owners.

Hannah
VP, Platform Reliability
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara@novapay.finance>, ops@novapay.finance, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-04T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident update and next steps — 2026-06-02 regional outage

Hello Sara / Daniel / NovaPay ops / Acme ops,

Thank you for your patience while we completed the internal review. Below is a concise customer-facing summary and the next steps we’re taking.

What happened (short):
- A third-party cloud provider experienced an interconnect failure that caused routing instability in US-EAST and intermittent impact in EU-WEST starting 07:47 UTC on 2026-06-02. That caused elevated error rates and connection resets for streaming workloads.

What we did:
- Immediately enabled cross-region diversion to healthy capacity (us-west, eu-central) and scaled critical pools.
- Tuned cache TTLs and temporarily disabled prefetch.
- Worked with the cloud provider; they have confirmed a partial networking misconfiguration that they are remediating.

Impact to you:
- NovaPay: transient errors and increased tail latency between 07:48–09:15 UTC; estimated customer-visible downtime ~1h 20m for a subset of sessions.
- Acme Retail: intermittent API timeouts in the same window.

What you can do now:
- If not already done, set DNS TTL=60s temporarily and add the following fallback hostnames to your routing policy: fallback.us-west.redwood.ai, fallback.eu-central.redwood.ai.
- If you want us to perform the reroute for you, reply and we’ll initiate a guided session.

Compensation & next steps:
- We will apply a prorated credit for service impact above 30 minutes; Lauren will follow up with exact numbers for your accounts.
- We’re delivering a fuller RCA and remediation plan (attached: rca-summary.pdf) and the final reroute configs used in the incident (reroute-configs.csv).
- Action owners: Marcus will deliver the health-check threshold change in 5 business days; Hannah is leading the roadmap item for automated pre-warm.

If you’d like a walk-through, I can set up a 30-minute call this week. Thank you again for flagging and for working with us through the incident.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
